framework.name: next
framework.notes: App Router at repo root (app/, no src/); route groups (marketing)/(auth)/(protected)/(docs); next.config.js is wrapped by withContentlayer (contentlayer2) and dynamically imports env.mjs, so the env schema is validated at config load.

node_or_python_requirement: not declared in package.json engines; .nvmrc = v16.18.0 (stale) while next@14.2.5 needs Node >=18.17.0; @types/node ^20

monorepo.notes: single Next.js app at repo root; pnpm-lock.yaml (440 KB) is the only lockfile, no pnpm-workspace.yaml

auth.notes: Auth.js v5 beta (next-auth 5.0.0-beta.19) with @auth/prisma-adapter; providers are Google OAuth + Resend magic-link only (no email+password, and no GitHub provider despite an unused sendVerificationRequest import in auth.config.ts). JWT session strategy; UserRole enum ADMIN|USER; middleware.ts re-exports auth from auth.ts instead of the adapter-free auth.config.ts.

search: cmdk command palette (client-side only, no server search)

env.notes: 14 of 15 are non-optional in env.mjs (@t3-oss/env-nextjs createEnv) and next.config.js imports env.mjs, so both `pnpm dev` and `pnpm build` throw before compiling unless all of them are set; only NEXTAUTH_URL is .optional(). .env.example (commented 'MySQL - Neon DB' but actually a postgres:// URL) lists the same set minus NEXTAUTH_URL; README says copy to .env.local, docs say .env - both gitignored. GITHUB_OAUTH_TOKEN is required yet used only for an optional GitHub star fetch.

deploy.notes: No Dockerfile, no docker-compose, no vercel.json, no `output: 'standalone'` in next.config.js, no .github/ directory. Deploy path is the Vercel button in README plus content/docs/installation.mdx (which itself warns the deploy fails until env vars are set). migrations_cmd is the command the docs give (content/docs/configuration/database.mdx); package.json has NO migrate/db script at all (scripts: dev, build, turbo, start, lint, preview, postinstall, email) and prisma/migrations/0_init is a baseline, not a migrate history. postinstall runs `prisma generate`.

tests.notes: No test runner and no test file anywhere: the 323-entry tree has no *.test.* / *.spec.* / __tests__ and no vitest/jest/playwright/cypress dependency or config; there is no .github/ directory at all, so no CI, issue templates or code scanning. Quality tooling is lint/format only (eslint + next/core-web-vitals, prettier + prettier-plugin-tailwindcss, commitlint, husky).

vendor.name: stripe
vendor.what_it_does: subscription checkout (mode: subscription), billing portal, and webhook sync of stripeCustomerId/stripeSubscriptionId/stripePriceId/stripeCurrentPeriodEnd onto the User row

vendor.name: resend
vendor.what_it_does: magic-link sign-in email delivery (Auth.js Resend provider) plus the React Email template
vendor.swap_target_hint: nodemailer/SMTP, postmark, or drop magic-link and keep Google OAuth

vendor.name: neon
vendor.what_it_does: hosted serverless Postgres behind DATABASE_URL (the Prisma datasource is plain postgresql, so Neon itself is not in the code)
vendor.swap_target_hint: any Postgres (Supabase, RDS, self-hosted) - no code change, only DATABASE_URL

vendor.name: vercel
vendor.what_it_does: hosting target, visitor analytics, and the edge ImageResponse OG image route
vendor.swap_target_hint: any Node host (Fly/VPS/Cloudflare) - needs a Dockerfile or `output: 'standalone'` you must add, plus replacing @vercel/og and @vercel/analytics

vendor.name: google-oauth
vendor.swap_target_hint: add/remove providers in auth.config.ts (an unused GITHUB_OAUTH_TOKEN already exists)

vendor.name: github-api
vendor.what_it_does: Authorization header for the landing-hero fetch of api.github.com star count
vendor.swap_target_hint: delete the fetch or hardcode a number

rebrand_surface.note: site name 'SaaS Starter', long description, mailSupport support@saas-starter.com, twitter/github links; footerLinks rows mostly href '#'
constructMetadata() defaults title/description/ogImage/favicon from siteConfig; used by nearly every page
name/short_name 'SaaS Starter' plus the android icon set
full favicon set, referenced by constructMetadata icons
static OG images carrying upstream branding; siteConfig.ogImage points at /_static/og.jpg

hardcoded h1 'Kick off with a bang with SaaS Starter', the 'Next.js 14, Prisma, Neon, Auth.js v5...' pitch, an upstream twitter announcement link, and the star fetch pinned to mickasmt/next-saas-stripe-starter
all shadcn CSS variables (baseColor neutral per components.json) - colors and dark mode live here
per-page titles hardcoded as '<Page> - SaaS Starter'
React Email magic-link template; siteName passed in from siteConfig

hardcoded_demo_content: landing page sections (components/sections/*) - audience/first-90-days marketing copy, screenshots and wording for a generic SaaS
6 fake testimonials in config/landing.ts (testimonials[]), rendered by components/sections/testimonials.tsx
4 demo blog posts in content/blog/*.mdx (Next.js/contentlayer topics) and 2 guides in content/guides/*.mdx, attributed to avatars mickasmt/shadcn
4 docs pages in content/docs/configuration/*.mdx that document this starter's own setup
/admin shows 4 identical InfoCard stat blocks plus two TransactionsList tables of the same hardcoded data, and /dashboard/charts renders 9 static recharts demos
/admin/orders is a static EmptyPlaceholder ('No orders listed') - its getCurrentUser()/ADMIN redirect is commented out
components/forms/newsletter-form.tsx only toasts the submitted JSON - no signup backend
content/pages/privacy.mdx and content/pages/terms.mdx boilerplate served through the /[slug] catch route

pitfalls.detail: env.mjs uses @t3-oss/env-nextjs createEnv with 14 non-optional vars (Google OAuth, DATABASE_URL, RESEND_API_KEY, STRIPE_API_KEY, the 4 Stripe price IDs, GITHUB_OAUTH_TOKEN...) and next.config.js does `import('./env.mjs')`, so the config load throws: `pnpm dev` and `pnpm build` both fail before compiling until every credential is present, and placeholder values still break Stripe/Resend at runtime. The repo's own install doc warns the Vercel deploy 'will fail'.
.nvmrc pins v16.18.0 but next@14.2.5 requires Node >= 18.17 - `nvm use` on a fresh clone hands you an unsupported runtime. Build with Node 20 (.nvmrc is simply stale).

README lists 'Framer Motion' under UI and a `use-debounce` hook among utilities; framer-motion is not in package.json and no .ts/.tsx file in the tree imports it (all 186 source files were fetched and grepped), so any motion work starts from zero.

husky@^9 with .husky/pre-commit (pretty-quick) and .husky/commit-msg (commitlint) exists, but package.json has no `prepare` script or husky install step, so the hooks are never wired on a fresh clone (and the files use the husky v8 shim style). Expect no git hooks despite the directory.

components/sections/hero-landing.tsx fetches https://api.github.com/repos/mickasmt/next-saas-stripe-starter at render time (next: {revalidate: 3600}) for the star count on '/'. Offline, rate-limited, or after a rebrand it returns an error body, stars is undefined, and nFormatter(undefined) renders into the hero; the URL is a hardcoded upstream reference.

/admin and /admin/orders are static mock UI, not features: OrdersPage's `redirect('/login')` + ADMIN check is commented out and prisma/schema.prisma has no Order model, so 'orders' must be built from scratch.
pitfalls.evidence: app/(protected)/admin/orders/page.tsx + prisma/schema.prisma (User, Account, Session, VerificationToken only)

pitfalls.detail: next is pinned exactly to 14.2.5, inside the affected range of CVE-2025-29927 (authorization bypass when the check lives in middleware; fixed in 14.2.25) and middleware.ts is the auth gate in this repo. next-auth is a 5.0.0-beta, and there has been no commit since 2024-07-26, so Next 15 / Auth.js 5 stable / React 19 upgrades are unassisted work.

middleware.ts re-exports `auth` from auth.ts (which imports PrismaAdapter and @prisma/client) instead of the edge-safe auth.config.ts that was split out for exactly that purpose - the Auth.js documented pattern. Not exercised here (repo never built), but a known source of Edge-runtime/Prisma bundling errors; auth.config.ts also carries a dead sendVerificationRequest import and a commented-out provider option.

contentlayer2/next-contentlayer2 (community fork of the unmaintained contentlayer) wraps next.config and generates .contentlayer/generated at dev/build time, but that directory is gitignored while tsconfig.json maps 'contentlayer/generated' and compiles contentlayer.config.ts - so a fresh clone's tsc/editor reports missing modules until a dev/build run creates it. sharp@^0.33.4 is the only native module (prebuilt binaries).

verdict.best_for: A single-tenant B2C/B2B SaaS that needs a polished marketing site, a role-gated dashboard and Stripe subscription billing on Next 14 App Router, when you will rebrand and extend it yourself rather than track upstream.
verdict.weak_for: Anything needing teams/orgs, i18n, uploads, background jobs, API keys or an audit trail - and any team that wants tests, CI or a maintained upgrade path (dormant since 2024-07-26, zero test files, zero workflows, beta Auth.js).
verdict.swap_burden: medium - Stripe/Resend/Neon/Vercel are thin and mostly config-swappable, but rebranding (every page, OG/favicons, hero copy), replacing the mock admin/orders pages, removing the upstream GitHub star fetch, and adding the missing tests/CI/Docker are all manual.

unmeasured: Nothing was installed, built or run (contract forbids it), so 'build-needs-env', the middleware/Prisma Edge concern and the husky-hook conclusion are read from source, not reproduced.
No dependency resolution was performed: peer conflicts between next-auth 5.0.0-beta.19 / react 18.3.1 / contentlayer2 0.5.x are unknown.
Non-TS code size: only .ts/.tsx lines were counted (12,534); CSS/MDX/JS sizes come from the languages API byte shares.
Runtime SaaS details (Stripe plan/price behaviour, live Neon/Vercel/Resend configuration) - out of scope; the billing page itself states it is a Stripe test-environment demo.
contributors is a single API page (4 accounts returned); 100+ contributor repos would need pagination, and contributors excludes anonymous/co-authored commits.
open_issues=26 is the API's open_issues_count (17 issues + 9 PRs); issues-only is 17. Both were measured and the combined figure is reported.
Repo settings not queried: branch protection, required status checks, dependabot/security alerts, traffic, wiki/discussions.

GitHub code search was rate-limited (403) at measurement time, so the 'no framer-motion / no i18n' findings rest on fetching and grepping all 186 .ts/.tsx files plus the config files, not on a server-side search over every extension.
Issue quality/triage was not assessed (only titles of the 5 most recent open items were sampled; one is a generic automated 'security audit' issue).
No test coverage exists to measure; complexity.loc_estimate is lines of code, not a quality metric.
